newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italian minister seeks flexibility on EMU tests.
newsitem.headline: Italian minister seeks flexibility on EMU tests.

text.p: Italian Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano said on Thursday that EU states should take into consideration any recession or economic slowdown when assessing in 1998 which states have respected the deficit criterion on qualifying for the single currency.

Speaking to Italian reporters on the sidelines of a European Union ministerial meeting, Napolitano said he agreed with former French President Valery Giscard d'Estaing and ex German Chancellor Helmut Schmidt who said that the effect of a recession on the deficit should be discounted.
"It is negative that we are not paying enough attention in Europe to the poor growth trend," Napolitano said.

"I believe that we must take into serious consideration Giscard d'Estaing's proposal, which was somewhat taken up by Helmut Schmidt...that we should also bear in mind in 1998, when the moment comes to calculate certain parameters -- such as the three percent budget deficit to GDP -- a recession or a growth slowdown." -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
